title: Recover pinned recipe selections across restarts
platforms: Linux / Xvfb isolated EUR interpreter; Windows GNU / Wine synthetic tests
changes: Preserve selected input roles using their anchored locations, kinds and content hashes; verify the input outside the frontend thread and check the restored selection before dispatch without repeating its completed selection command.
Record stable pin fingerprints in status observations so a temporary catalog ID may change across runs; explicit refresh remains necessary for a new catalog index or cheat snapshot.
validation: Linux synthetic regression passed 37 recipe, 36 control, 4 completion, 4 registry and 1 portable-move selection test; Windows GNU/Wine passed 37, 37, 4, 4 and 1 respectively.

An isolated Linux/Xvfb interpreter recovered a synthetic catalog selection through two normal restarts and three distinct control runs; the temporary ID changed, stable pin and completed results remained unchanged, one later frame ran, and a second resume had no effect. Protected inputs stayed unchanged.
limitations: Up to three selected roles and 2 KiB of pin metadata are supported; older selection results without pins, earlier collectors, ambiguous pending actions and stale or unavailable inputs are refused. No continuous filesystem watch exists between recovery verification and later action preflight.
The real proof used simulated cancellation and silent audio; real Wine restart, native Windows and physical input remain open.
